subject: Investigation: intermittent timeouts reported for /v1/generate — triage & closure
messages:
From: Alex Harris <alex.harris@acme-retail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: SLA Team <sla@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 18:23:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent timeouts hitting /v1/generate — user-facing 504s

Hi Rachel,

We're seeing intermittent 504/timeouts when our frontend calls your /v1/generate endpoint. First noticed around 18:15 PST — multiple users reported the same thing and we saw a small spike in our error rate. Sample request IDs: req_9f2a1c, req_9f2a7d.

What we observed:
- Requests returned 504 after ~30s
- Happened in us-west-2 region only (we're routed there)
- Not all requests were affected; roughly 2-3% of calls in a 10m window

I've attached a short HAR and a screenshot from our Sentry trace. Can you confirm whether anything was happening on your side around that time? We need to know if this was a Redwood outage or something on our gateway.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Harris
VP Engineering, Acme Retail
alex.harris@acme-retail.com

Attachments: screenshot-504.png, acme-har-20260216.har

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Harris <alex.harris@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 18:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent timeouts hitting /v1/generate — user-facing 504s

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts.

We're sorry you saw those timeouts. I'm looping in Marissa from our support/infra team to triage immediately. Can you confirm:
1) The model and model version you were calling (model param in your request)
2) Approximate request payload size (token count) for req_9f2a1c
3) Whether you're using any proxy or API gateway that might impose its own timeouts

We'll start by checking our serving logs and infra metrics for the 18:00–18:30 PST window and report back within 4 hours. If this looks like an internal issue we'll treat it as a Sev 2.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 02:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: triage notes for Acme — no reproduction in our cluster

Internal triage summary (attempted 3/17 01:00–03:30 UTC):
- Checked host and model logs for us-west-2 for 2026-02-16 02:00–03:00 UTC (maps to the 18:00 PST window). No 5xx or 504 returned by our frontends or model servers.
- Reviewed autoscaler and GPU utilization: no saturation events, CPU and memory within normal bounds.
- Ran controlled replay of sample payloads using the request IDs provided. Replayed 50 identical requests over a 15m window from our test harness; all completed with 200 and median latency equal to baseline.
- Kept connection-level monitoring (ELB + envoy) open — there was a transient increase in client-side connection resets from a small set of client IPs (likely a network path). No evidence of backend timeouts.

Attachments: attached acme-request-logs-20260216.zip (server-side request logs filtered by request id), triage-screenshot-epoch.png (latency graph).

Conclusion: at this time we cannot reproduce the 504s from Redwood's side. The pattern looks like it may be network/proxy related at the customer edge or gateway timeouts. Suggested next steps:
- Ask Acme to share gateway/proxy timeout configs and any rate-limiter logs for the same timestamp.
- If Acme can run a brief controlled test specifying model, token counts, and request rate we can replay simultaneously to capture packet traces.

If leadership wants, we can keep this open as a monitoring ticket for 48 hours and add an alert for any 5xx spikes in us-west-2.

— Marissa
Senior Support Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Harris <alex.harris@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent timeouts hitting /v1/generate — triage & closure

Hi Alex — quick update and closure.

Thanks for the quick reply and the additional gateway configs you sent overnight. Per Marissa's triage below and the logs we've shared (attached), we did not find any server-side errors or capacity limits in our us-west-2 fleet that would produce 504s during the 18:15 PST window on 2026-02-16. Our replayed requests completed normally.

What we did find that may explain the symptoms:
- Your gateway has an idle-connection timeout of 28s which can surface as 504s on the client when paired with transient packet loss.
- A small subset of client IPs showed connection resets during the window (see attached filtered logs).

Action taken by Redwood:
- We reviewed serving metrics and no fallback or model restart events were triggered.
- We added a temporary alert on 5xx/504 deviation in us-west-2 for the next 72 hours.
- Uploaded triage artifacts and a short runbook to our shared folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/triage-acme-20260216 (read-only link).

Recommended next steps for Acme:
1) Increase gateway idle timeout to 45s or wire a keepalive for long-running requests.
2) Run a coordinated replay (we can provide a script) so we can capture packet traces simultaneously if this reappears.
3) If you see recurrence after those changes, reopen this thread and we'll escalate to an on-call engineer immediately.

Closing the ticket on our side for now — please reopen if you observe further user-facing 504s.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

Attachments: acme-request-logs-20260216.zip, triage-screenshot-epoch.png
